Attendees: Laura Chen (Redwood AE), Marco Ruiz (Redwood SE), Jamal Price (Redwood SE), Nina Patel (Astra Head of ML), Rafael Gomez (Astra CTO), Sana Iqbal (Astra Infra Lead), Tom Ellis (Astra Product)

deployment mode tradeoffs: Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (VPC/on-prem)
transcript:
[00:00] Laura: Hey everyone, thanks for hopping on. this is Laura from Redwood, with Marco and Jamal. quick intro round?
[00:10] Nina: Hi I'm Nina, head of ML at Astra. we've been evaluating options for running LLMs across product and risk teams.
[00:18] Rafael: Rafael here, CTO. high level we need something that meets compliance for PII and has lowish latency for customer-facing flows.
[00:25] Marco: Great, appreciate that. to set expectations, we'll cover model choices, context lengths, multilingual support, and deployment options. any must-haves up front?
[00:36] Sana: Data residency + audit logs are musts. also KMS integration for keys.
[00:42] Jamal: Noted. Nina, can you describe a typical prompt or document you need to keep in context?
[00:50] Nina: Sure — think regulatory filings and multi-year statements, often 15–30 pages, dozens of tables; sometimes we want to pass a full financial packet and then ask multi-step Q&A. so effective context is large, 128k would be ideal long-term, but we're ok with incremental approaches.
[01:15] Marco: OK that helps. so two immediate options: use hosted Redwood with prefix/KV caching for repeated doc fragments, or Dedicated/Private with larger context tokens and pinned model variants.
[01:28] Rafael: Latency tradeoff is key. customer-facing summary must be under 500ms tail p95 ideally. is that realistic with 32k/64k contexts?
[01:40] Marco: With batching and GPU-optimized kernels we can hit sub-second for many workloads, but 128k brings compute cost up and some extra latency. we typically recommend caching long document embeddings and only streaming missing chunks, that reduces tokens and cost.
[01:55] Nina: Can you talk about open models — we've run Llama2 and Mistral in-house a bit. curious about Redwood-verified models and quantization options.
[02:05] Jamal: Sure. Redwood maintains a catalog of verified open models, we profile latency, throughput, and quality on common fin prompts. for cost we support int8/int4 quantization paths — Q8 and Q4 — and tradeoffs vary by model. e.g. Llama2-70B Q8 is cheaper than full fp16 and often similar quality after finetune; Mistral-Instruct variants can be faster but some hallucination modes change.
[02:30] Tom: tool-calling is another must for us — we need structured outputs that trigger downstream workflows (create ticket, call risk engine). how does Redwood support tool-calling?
[02:40] Marco: We have function/tool calling primitives in the hosted API — you can define schemas and Redwood streams structured JSON; at Dedicated/Private you get the same interface with routing policies. we also support hybrid retrieval toolchain where you call an internal service and pass back results to the model.
[02:55] Nina: How deterministic is tool-calling across quantized models? we've seen schema drift when responses slip.
[03:02] Jamal: Good point. we recommend a lightweight response validator layer — Redwood can enforce strict schema return or fallback to a deterministic reranker. with quantized models we usually do a small n-shot prompt plus a schema post-check.
[03:15] Rafael: On compliance: can you run Private (VPC) with KMS/HSM and full audit logs? our legal team wants separation for production data.
[03:24] Laura: Yes. Redwood Private supports customer-managed VPC deployment and KMS integration (we've done HSM partners). audit logs and extended retention are available as an enterprise add-on. we'll share the security pack after the call.
[03:36] Sana: For pilot, we want to see concrete metrics: token cost per query, p50/p95 latency, and failure modes. also result quality — e.g. precision on entity extraction in financial tables.
[03:48] Marco: We'll run three-model benchmarks against your sample prompt set: Llama2-70B Q8, Mistral-Instruct-large, and RedGem-13B (a smaller low-latency variant). we'll include cost estimates and a spreadsheet with token breakdowns.
[04:05] Nina: RedGem? is that internal or a community model?
[04:08] Jamal: it's in our catalog — curated open model variant that we use for lower-latency routing. name might show up slightly different in the docs, sorry if I mangle it.
[04:17] Tom: multilingual — some regulatory docs are in Spanish and Portuguese. do you support tokenizers and normalization for those?
[04:23] Marco: Yes, our runtime supports multilingual tokenization and we profile per-language quality. for finance-specific Spanish we recommend fine-tuning or instruction tuning on your corpus. you can also route Spanish requests to a model variant optimized for multilingual understanding.
[04:37] Rafael: What about data retention for hosted? we cannot retain PII or raw documents in-hosted environment.
[04:44] Laura: Hosted can be configured with no-persist options and strict retention windows; for many customers with strict requirements we recommend Dedicated or Private where you own the storage. we'll detail the retention controls in the security doc.
[04:56] Nina: Can we run a small POC on hosted first to validate the pipeline then move to Dedicated?
[05:02] Laura: That's a common approach. many teams do hosted pilot to iterate fast, then move to Dedicated for scale and finally Private for compliance. pricing and performance vary — we'll lay that out in the spreadsheet.
[05:12] Sana: Our infra wants to test VPC peering and egress rules. is there a network diagram for Private deployments?
[05:18] Jamal: We'll send a standard Private deployment topology with peering, NAT, and recommended firewall rules. expect that in the security pack.
[05:25] Rafael: Any gotchas on model rollouts? can we pin model versions for a route?
[05:31] Marco: Yep. Redwood supports version pinning, canary rollouts, and automatic fallback to older model variants if there's regression. helpful for controlled rollouts across environments.
[05:42] Tom: what's the cadence and support model for updates? we can't have sudden breaking performance changes.
[05:47] Laura: enterprise customers get changelogs and optional update windows; we also provide regression monitoring hooks tied to your evals.
[05:56] Nina: On the bench: we care about hallucination in table extraction especially — please include precision/recall metrics vs our labeled set.
[06:04] Marco: Absolutely. include confusion matrix and sample failures. we'll also show token-level cost and latency for the typical prompt sizes you share.
[06:12] Rafael: timeline-wise we want pilot in two weeks, full evaluation within 6 weeks. is that feasible?
[06:18] Laura: Two-week pilot kickoff is tight but doable if we get prompts and sample data today/soon. SE bench by two weeks after kickoff.
[06:25] Nina: I'll upload a sample deck and prompt set to the shared folder after this call. also legal will want the SOC2 and right to audit wording.
[06:33] Laura: Noted — we'll include audit wording options.
[06:36] [12:15] (partial audio glitch) Speaker 2: sorry I missed that last bit, can you repeat the KMS flow?
[12:20] Jamal: Sure — in Private you bring your KMS; Redwood integrates via standard envelope encryption and we never persist your plaintext keys. in Dedicated we offer a managed KMS option or customer KMS via peering.
[12:34] [20:05] Marco: Quick note on KV cache: for long docs we store intermediate KV snapshots to avoid reprocessing full context, that reduces token recompute and cost — it's transparent to the API.
[20:18] Nina: what's the security of KV cache? could cached segments leak across tenants?
[20:23] Jamal: No cross-tenant leakage; caches are tenant-scoped and in Private/Dedicated can be placed on customer storage.
[20:30] Rafael: Any example customers in finance?
[20:33] Laura: We can't name all without NDA but have case studies in payments and wealth platforms; we'll share relevant references if you want.
[20:40] Tom: About model quantization — do you see schema drift more in INT4 vs INT8?
[20:45] Marco: INT4 can introduce more variability; for structured output we lean to INT8 or QAT (quant aware tuning) to reduce schema risk.
[20:53] Nina: Ok that's helpful. pricing ballpark? hosted vs dedicated vs private?
[20:58] Laura: We'll send an apples-to-apples estimate: hosted is lowest setup but higher per-token; dedicated is predictable monthly commit with lower per-token; private has platform fees + infra; we'll put ranges in the follow-up.
[21:10] Rafael: can you show us sample prompts for the bench?
[21:13] Marco: We'll use your labeled set plus a synthetic set for edge cases.
[21:20] Nina: Great. any blockers we should address now?
[21:23] Sana: We need the network diagram, security pack, and sample bench spreadsheet.
[21:28] Laura: We'll get those out. thanks all. shall we recap next steps?
[21:33] Nina: yes please.
[21:35] Laura: Recap: Redwood sends security pack + network diagram by 8/12; SE runs model bench and shares spreadsheet by 8/20; schedule pilot kickoff week of 8/25; Astra to upload prompt set by end of day 8/9.
[21:50] Rafael: sounds good. thanks everyone.
[21:52] Tom: thanks!
[21:54] [end]
